DK26.6 is a specific medical diagnosis code representing a chronic or unspecified duodenal ulcer accompanied by both bleeding and perforation [^src3]. Within the Danish healthcare system, this code plays a critical role in monitoring patient safety and treatment outcomes, particularly for individuals managing cardiovascular conditions. 

Specifically, DK26.6 is utilized as part of a comprehensive set of diagnostic codes to track the incidence of [[alvorlig-bloedning|Alvorlig blødning]] (severe bleeding) among patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren|atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation) [^src3]. Because patients with atrial fibrillation are often prescribed anticoagulant medications, monitoring severe bleeding events—including gastrointestinal complications like those indicated by DK26.6—is a key clinical quality indicator evaluated in national annual reports [^src2]. 

To accurately capture these adverse events, the national clinical quality database employs a broad spectrum of diagnostic codes. The indicator for severe bleeding encompasses codes for intracranial hemorrhage (DI60–DS066), gastrointestinal bleeding (including DK26.6 alongside others like DK25.0–DK29.8A and DK92.0–DK92.2), and bleeding in the urinary or respiratory tracts (such as DJ942, DN02, DR04, and DR31) [^src1]. By systematically recording DK26.6 and related codes, health authorities can evaluate the risks associated with atrial fibrillation treatments and improve clinical guidelines across Denmark's regions [^src1].
